extracted.intended_audience: independent public accountants auditing SBICs; SBIC management and boards responsible for financial reporting and compliance with SBA rules
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive audit and reporting standards for Small Business Investment Companies (SBICs), covering verification, valuation, disclosures, bonding, recognition of income/gains, and preparation of SBA Financial Report (Form 468). Targeted to auditors and SBIC management to ensure SBA regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for uncollectible loans and losses on debt securities
rubrics_metrics.description: The allowance for uncollectible loans and the allowance for losses on debt securities should be reviewed as to adequacy and commented upon in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If considered desirable, adjusting entries to the allowance accounts should be recommended by the accountant for adoption by the SBIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of unearned discounts, fees, and charges deducted from principal
rubrics_metrics.description: Special attention should be given by the accountant to verification of all amounts of unearned discount, fees, and other charges shown as deducted from the unpaid principal balances of loans and debt securities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of capital stock of small business concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: All capital stock of small business concerns in the possession of the SBIC should be verified by inspection of the stock certificates; similar stock not in possession should be confirmed by direct correspondence with those having possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capital stock of small business concerns is to be recorded on the books of the SBIC at cost. When participations are sold to others, only the portion retained by the selling company is shown in the seller’s books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of cost determinations for warrants/options/stock rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The independent public accountant should review the cost determinations made with respect to warrants, options, or other stock rights carried on the books at a monetary value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the selling company’s portion is shown when participations are sold to others. Accountant should inspect agreements and documents evidencing participations and request confirmations from sellers as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and confirmation of participation agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Accountant should inspect agreements and other documents evidencing each participation purchased and should request confirmation from sellers to the extent considered necessary; subsidiary records reflecting participations of others should be reviewed against participation agreements and confirmed with purchasers when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board responsibility for valuation of stock and stock rights
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of the SBIC’s board of directors to determine in good faith a realistic valuation for each capital stock investment and for warrants, options, or other stock rights for which a separate cost has been determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuation shall be arrived at after consideration of all pertinent factors; valuation techniques and standards are set forth in SBA Policy and Procedural Release No. 2006 (Dec 31, 1965).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountant's duty to satisfy reasonableness of board valuations
rubrics_metrics.description: The independent public accountant should satisfy himself as to the reasonableness of the bases employed by the board of directors in making the value determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No appreciation in the value of capital stock or stock rights is to be recorded in the books of account. Valuations determined by the board are to be shown in the memorandum column of the applicable schedule of the Financial Report, SBA Form 468.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of material decreases in value of capital stock/stock rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Any material decrease in value of capital stock or stock rights, as determined by the board of directors, that is not obviously of a transitory nature should be compensated for by an increase in the allowance for losses on capital stock or on warrants/options/stock rights, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These allowance accounts should be reviewed as to adequacy and commented upon in the accountant's report. Adjusting entries to effect necessary increases should be recommended; entries should be recommended to write off any established loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venture capital amount verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The independent public accountant, referring to the official definition of venture capital and reviewing the lending instruments and related documents, should determine that the total amount of venture capital as indicated in the Financial Report, SBA Form 468, is substantially correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the Small Business Investment Act, SBICs must maintain a minimum percentage of funds in venture capital per regulations (section 107.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording assets acquired in liquidation of loans and debt securities
rubrics_metrics.description: Property taken in liquidation should be recorded at an amount determined by the board of directors on the basis of bid-in price, agreed consideration, or fair appraised value as deemed most suitable, provided that the net amount recorded shall not exceed the total amount of the related loan or equity security indebtedness involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For mortgaged real property, record at gross value as determined by the board, reduced as necessary to bring net recorded value within the limitation. Include existing mortgages among SBIC liabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification procedures for assets acquired in liquidation
rubrics_metrics.description: The accountant should verify each asset through application of procedures generally accepted for audit of the particular class of assets involved and ascertain board authorization for recording these assets at the amounts shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amount recorded will correctly represent only the selling company’s portion of any such assets in which participations are sold to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on recording appreciation for assets acquired in liquidation
rubrics_metrics.description: No appreciation in the original recorded value of assets acquired in liquidation of loans and debt securities is to be recorded in the books of account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuations as determined by the board are to be shown in the memorandum column of the applicable schedule of the Financial Report, SBA Form 468, and considered in developing the memorandum item following the Statement of Financial Condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of accumulated depreciation on assets acquired in liquidation
rubrics_metrics.description: The accumulated depreciation on assets acquired in liquidation should be reviewed by the accountant to assure that it is not less in amount than a conservative estimate of the expired service life of such property while owned by the SBIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insurance coverage on such assets should also be reviewed as to adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion and write-off recommendation for acquired assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquired assets should be discussed with executive officers; writeoff should be recommended for items considered worthless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The allowance for losses on assets acquired in liquidation should be reviewed for adequacy and commented upon in the report; adjusting entries recommended if desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of title and recording basis for corporate premises
rubrics_metrics.description: During the first audit, the independent public accountant should examine the documents showing title to corporate premises and ascertain that land is carried at acquisition cost plus cost of subsequent benefit assessments and improvements (other than buildings), and that buildings are recorded at acquisition cost plus cost of subsequent improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify basis for recorded cost; check capital additions to ensure only properly capitalizable items were added; examine vouchers and invoices; review retirements and sales; insurance coverage adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review accumulated depreciation for corporate premises
rubrics_metrics.description: The accumulated depreciation on the building and related improvements should be reviewed to assure that it is not less than a conservative estimate of the expired service life of such building and improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards when sharing premises with other institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an SBIC operates in the same or communicating office or building with a bank or other financial institution, the accountant should satisfy himself that safeguards are maintained which effectively segregate the books, records, and assets of the separate institutions at all times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditor report on corporate premises
rubrics_metrics.description: The audit findings concerning corporate premises owned should be set forth in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and verification of furniture and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: The accountant should ascertain that furniture and equipment, including automobiles, are recorded on the books at cost; inspect ownership documents for automobiles and examine invoices for major additions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test sales and trade-ins to ensure proper recording; review insurance coverage adequacy; accumulated depreciation on furniture and equipment should be reviewed for adequacy; report should comment on unusual conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit of organization costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal fees, promotional expense, stock certificate costs, incorporation fees, taxes, and other charges comprising organization costs should be audited for propriety as capital charges pending amortization or writeoff to the organization expense account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the first audit, review basis for amortization and consistency of planned elimination; first audit report should describe components of this asset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of other long-term and deferred items
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts relating to long-term notes receivable, leasehold improvements, supplies on hand, insurance prepayments, and other prepayments and deferred items should be reviewed for propriety, applicability to future periods, and appropriateness of the basis for writeoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take particular note of any amounts deferred due to improper accounting or failure to identify correct purposes. Accountant should prepare summary of insurance coverage for inclusion in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalized improvements to leased property
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvements to leased property used as the company’s office quarters should be checked against invoices, contracts, and supporting documents to ensure they are properly capitalizable and that writeoff accounting is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The audit report should contain adequate information on prepayments and deferred charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of miscellaneous assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Miscellaneous assets not included under other captions, including recoverable amounts (loans or equity financing advanced for protection and preservation of investments), should be reviewed for validity and for propriety of their retention on the books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and reconciliation of accounts payable related to participations
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts payable for participating companies' portions of principal and accrued interest receivable from financed small business concerns, compensation for services rendered on participations purchased, commitment fees on deferred participations by others, and other values shown by subsidiary records should be verified and reconciled to control accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accruals for compensation payable and commitment fees payable should be reviewed with reference to participation agreements. Unusually large amounts and a reasonable proportion of other amounts due on open account should be confirmed by correspondence with creditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of other current and accrued liabilities and contingent liabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsidiary records on other current and accrued liabilities should be checked and reconciled with control accounts. A certificate signed by an executive officer should be obtained stating all actual liabilities have been entered and contingent liabilities reported. The accountant should communicate with the SBIC’s attorney to determine existence of claims for establishing contingent liabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accountant should state in the report that certificates were received from the executive officer and the attorney. The report should present pertinent information concerning unusual current and accrued liabilities. Special attention to amounts due directors, officers, employees, and to contingent liabilities including commitments and guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation and confirmation of indebtedness to SBA
rubrics_metrics.description: Indebtedness to SBA should be reconciled to the current statements from the Small Business Administration. Direct confirmation from SBA is required and should be requested by submission of a triplicate statement showing unpaid balances of principal and interest at the balance sheet date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequate identification of each obligation, using execution date and SBA loan symbols, should be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation of debt to others and review of loan documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt to others than SBA for funds borrowed should be confirmed by correspondence; loan agreements, contracts, mortgages, and minutes of board meetings pertaining thereto should be examined to determine compliance with terms bearing on the financial position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity check of other liabilities and deferred credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Other liabilities and deferred credits should be checked for validity; if material, appropriate comments should be included in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special attention to amounts due directors, officers, and employees and to contingent liabilities, including commitments and guarantees. Accountant should ensure Form 468 schedules reflect all commitments, guaranteed obligations, and contingent liabilities, with totals shown as a footnote on page 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of capital stock transactions and related disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification of capital stock should be carried out by examination of stock records and certificate books or by direct confirmation from registrar/transfer agent; cash records showing consideration received should be reviewed; authorizations, charter and bylaws referred to; existence of stock options, warrants, conversion privileges, special terms assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all such transactions are appropriately recorded and presented in financial statements, notes, or schedules. Disclose arrearages in payments on subscribed capital stock or dividends, analyze treasury stock transactions, and provide informative comments regarding capital stock transactions in the audit report. Review changes in surplus accounts for propriety and classification of realized income vs realized gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loans and investments valuation and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Review should be made of the valuation of loans and investments. The independent public accountant should determine and report whether the SBIC has followed instructions for the memorandum item following the Statement of Financial Condition in SBA Form 468 in making the valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is understood that the accountant’s opinion on the financial statements does not extend to the valuation of loans and investments given in such memorandum item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests of income/expense and gain/loss accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate tests should be made of income and expense and gain and loss accounts for the period under review sufficient to satisfy the accountant that transactions summarized are genuine and properly authorized and accurately recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification procedures should be based on the same test principles as applied to balance sheet accounts. After examining representative transactions, scan accounts and examine unusual entries. Special attention to transactions contributing to recorded gain or loss on sales of investments. Refer to SBA requirements concerning realization and use of income and gains (Addendum I). Include in comments the last year through which federal income tax returns of the SBIC have been audited by IRS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for fidelity bond (Addendum I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee shall obtain a fidelity bond executed by an acceptable surety; each officer and employee who has control over or access to cash or other property must be covered by such fidelity bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bond must be executed by surety holding a certificate of authority from the Secretary of the Treasury as acceptable surety on federal bonds and must meet other provisions specified in Addendum I (parts 2 and 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of fidelity bond required
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee shall be covered by a Brokers Blanket Bond, Standard Form No. 14. A Licensee may be covered by Bankers Blanket Bond, Standard Form No. 24, if it meets paragraph 3 provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general, riders to standard form bonds are unacceptable unless they patently increase benefits. SBA has listed specific riders to Form 14 that are unacceptable (SR 5307 valuation clause, SR 5568 discovery rider (Form 14), SR 5571 Rider-Discovery Form, SR 5771 Rights after Termination or Cancellation, SR 5301 Delete Misplacement Rider).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bank majority-ownership bonding exception
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee majority-owned (more than 50%) by commercial banks that are FDIC members, or by a bank holding company whose subsidiaries are FDIC members, may be included as a joint insured under Bankers Blanket Bond, Standard Form No. 24, which insures the parent bank(s) or holding company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If coverage under Form 24 is restricted by deductible insuring clauses that would apply to the Licensee, a Brokers Blanket Bond (Form 14) must be employed to furnish coverage for deductible amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval by bank directors for joint insured status
rubrics_metrics.description: Board of directors of the commercial bank(s) or bank holding company must approve extending the Bankers Blanket Bond (Form 24) to include the Licensee as a joint insured and must approve any Brokers Blanket Bond (Form 14) needed to furnish coverage for deductibles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certified copy of the minutes of the meeting(s) at which such bond(s) were approved shall be retained in the permanent records of the Licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee board approval and issuer certification for bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: The board of directors of the Licensee must approve the fidelity bond(s); a certified copy of the minutes must be retained. The Licensee must obtain from the issuer a statement in writing certifying that the bonds fulfill the requirements to the issuer's knowledge and belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellations and claims notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee must notify SBA at least 30 days prior to any request to the surety to terminate, cancel or otherwise revoke the bond; each Licensee shall have as a condition of a certified bond a rider requiring the surety to notify SBA at least 30 days in advance of effective date of cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Licensee shall immediately in writing notify SBA of any claim for loss filed under the bond with the surety. Notifications to SBA must be by certified mail addressed to the Associate Administrator for Investment, Small Business Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum fidelity bond coverage amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum bond amount for each Licensee acceptable to SBA shall be based upon total assets plus unpaid balance of loans and investments serviced for others, with a tiered schedule (e.g., up to $400,000 = $25,000; $400,001–$750,000 = $40,000; etc.) and formula for amounts over $10,000,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For $10,000,001 and over the minimum is $200,000 plus $10,000 for each $1 million or fraction thereof over $10 million, except no Licensee shall be required to provide a bond greater than $1 million.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bank custodian fidelity bond exception
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Licensee’s portfolio securities are held by a commercial bank (FDIC member) as custodian under a custodianship agreement, the bank’s fidelity bond may be construed as furnishing adequate surety protection for securities and funds in its custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided that the amount of assets in possession of the Licensee at any one time, or $400,000 (whichever is greater), is covered by a Brokers Blanket Bond (Form 14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Addendum II — realization and use of income/gains
rubrics_metrics.description: Addendum II provides guidance to SBICs for determination of realization of operating income and gains on investments and the use of such profits for various corporate purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of income from operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees may, provided collection is reasonably assured, treat income from dividends and fees as realized when a transaction is effected in the ordinary course of business; treat commitment income and interest income as realized when a transaction is effected or through the passage of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of gains from sales of assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Gains from sales of assets (portfolio securities, assets acquired in liquidation, other assets) qualify as realized gain only when the sale represents a final transaction under specified rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portion of cash installment payments representing gain may be recognized immediately as such payments are received when installment feature is all that prevents characterization as final. Any transaction with recourse upon the Licensee or involving understandings/rights to repurchase/resell shall not be considered final. Any reacquisition by the Licensee nullifies finality. Gains not qualifying as realized must be deferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses of realized profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Only profits realized in accordance with the rules may be used for obtaining loan funds from SBA, used for payment of dividends, or treated as realized profits for improvement of bargaining position in mergers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profits realized may also be used for correcting capital impairment. Noncash gain on sale to a bona fide purchaser, which has been deferred, may be recognized by SBA for correcting capital impairment subject to SBA approval and prudence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances raising serious question about recognition of noncash gain
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances that would raise serious question as to the propriety of current recognition of gain include (1) assets received consist of unquoted stock or noncash property which cannot be reasonably evaluated; (2) evidence of purchaser financial weakness; (3) uncertainty as to costs/expenses to be incurred; (4) substantial uncertainty as to proceeds because of form of consideration or method of settlement (nonrecourse notes, non-interest-bearing notes, purchaser’s stock, optional settlement provisions); (5) indeterminate amount/time of payment dependent on future events; (6) retention of effective control of asset by Licensee; (7) limitations on purchaser’s profits or on development/disposition of asset; (8) simultaneous sale and repurchase by same/affiliated interests; (9) concurrent loan to or financing of purchaser; (10) small or no down payment; (11) simultaneous sale and leaseback of asset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for obtaining SBA recognition of noncash gain
rubrics_metrics.description: Gain on sale that represents a final transaction may be recognized as realized gain immediately when received in cash or acceptable equivalents. The Licensee should submit to SBA, in triplicate, a summary statement identifying each sale transaction with particulars: (a) portfolio securities/assets parted with and their cost less allowance for losses, proceeds obtained, net gain or loss; (b) name of purchaser and affiliation; (c) description and value of consideration received, including terms and collateral; (d) provisions of any rights or privileges obtained or granted by the Licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable forms of immediate recognition include money, checks, negotiable CDs issued by FDIC banks, and negotiable direct obligations of the U.S. Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting requirements for realized and deferred gains
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on classification of income as realized and procedures when amounts are not considered realized are found in notes to income accounts Nos. 500, 512, 516, 532 in the System of Account Classifications for SBICs (Part III of the regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any profit not qualifying as realized gain should be credited to account No. 383, Other Deferred Credits, pending realization. SBA recognition of noncash gain does not itself authorize transfer from account No. 383 to gain accounts; transfer depends on meeting qualifications in section 2.b. of the addendum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of valuation and memorandum items in Form 468
rubrics_metrics.description: Valuations determined by the board of directors are to be shown in the memorandum column of the applicable schedule of the Financial Report (SBA Form 468) and taken into consideration in developing the memorandum item following the Statement of Financial Condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accountant should determine whether SBIC followed instructions for the memorandum item; accountant's opinion does not extend to valuation in the memorandum.
